key_insight: AEAPTMS amino-silane passivation makes mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform and stable, as shown by narrower dark CPD and higher, faster-settling surface photovoltage.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to reduce interfacial voltage losses and improve carrier landscape uniformity in perovskite solar cells without needing obvious morphological changes.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on thin films
Compare dark CPD and illuminated SPV before vs. after AEAPTMS passivation
Grain-boundary vs. grain-interior SPV analysis plus wavelength-dependent measurements
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed the dark CPD distribution from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the SPV stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: The reported benefits are nanoscale thin-film measurements, so translation to full devices and long-term operational stability still needs validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
